title: Contains Duplicate
description: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return false if every element is distinct.
hints: Use a Hash Set to detect duplicates in O(N) time.

title: Missing Number
description: Given an array nums containing n distinct numbers in the range [0, n], return the only number in the range that is missing from the array.
hints: You can use the math formula for the sum of the first n numbers: n*(n+1)/2. The missing number is the difference between this and the actual sum.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description: You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the i-th day. You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and choosing a different day in the future to sell that stock.
hints: Track the minimum price seen so far and continuously update the maximum possible profit at each day.

title: Maximum Subarray
description: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum and return its sum.
hints: Use Kadane's Algorithm. Keep a running sum, and if it ever goes negative, reset it to 0 because a negative sum will only actively hurt future sums.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i]. You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and without using the division operation.
hints: Compute prefix products from left-to-right, then suffix products from right-to-left. Multiply them together for the answer.

hints: Sort the array first. Then iterate through the array, setting the current item as targets and using the Two Pointer approach on the remaining subarray to find sums corresponding to 0.

title: Container With Most Water
description: You are given an integer array height of length n. There are n vertical lines drawn. Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container, such that the container contains the most water.
hints: Use completely opposite Two Pointers (left = 0, right = end). Calculate area, then move the pointer that points to the shorter line inward.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
description: Suppose an array of length n sorted in ascending order is rotated between 1 and n times. Find the minimum element of this array. Must run in O(log n) time.
hints: Because it runs in O(log N), use modified Binary Search. If the mid element is greater than the rightmost element, the minimum is isolated in the right half.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array

hints: Modified Binary Search. Check if the left half is strictly sorted. If target lies within it, search left. Otherwise search right.

title: First Missing Positive
description:
Given an unsorted integer array `nums`, return the smallest missing positive integer.

You must implement an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and uses O(1) auxiliary space.
hints: The answer must be in the range [1, n+1] where n is the length of the array.
Use the array itself as a hash map. For each number x in range [1, n], place it at index x-1.
After rearranging, scan the array: the first index i where nums[i] != i+1 gives the answer i+1. If all positions are correct, the answer is n+1.

title: Jump Game II
description:
You are given a 0-indexed array of integers `nums` of length `n`. You are initially at `nums[0]`.

Each element `nums[i]` represents the maximum length of a forward jump from index `i`. In other words, if you are at `nums[i]`, you can jump to any `nums[i + j]` where `0 <= j <= nums[i]` and `i + j < n`.

Return the minimum number of jumps to reach `nums[n - 1]`. The test cases are generated so that you can always reach `nums[n - 1]`.
constraints: The generated input is such that you can always reach the last index.
hints: Greedy approach: at each step, track the farthest index reachable with the current number of jumps.
Use two pointers: `curEnd` (the farthest you can reach with current jumps) and `farthest` (the farthest reachable if you take one more jump).
When you reach `curEnd`, increment jumps and set `curEnd = farthest`. Stop when `curEnd >= n-1`.
